npcs.quote: I don't read Latin. Tell me if it's worth money.

meta.worldTruth: A document's value is what someone will pay for it, not what it says.

impartial: "I don't read Latin. Tell me if it's worth money."
questActive: "Take it to the archivist. Back by prime. In one piece."
friendly: "Hamburg contact sent three of these last season. Two were worth nothing. One was not."
dearFriend: "You read it correctly. That's the only thing that matters in this business."

npcs.quote: Format class confirmed. The seal narrows the date. That's what I can give you.

meta.worldTruth: Provenance is established by pattern, not by claim.
meta.enemy: Couriers who present originals without documentation of transit.

impartial: "Format class confirmed. The seal narrows the date. That's what I can give you."
questActive: "Cross-reference against the Hamburg index. I'll log the format class match."
friendly: "The Hansa archive holds three copies of English ecclesiastical records from the 1520s. This matches the pattern."
dearFriend: "Logged. Seal impression consistent, 1527 to 1529. That's the closest I can get to authenticated."

npcs.quote: The category is what survives when the object is gone. We are building the category.

meta.worldTruth: Every document is a record of the moment it became necessary to write something down.
meta.enemy: Archivists who categorize by medium rather than by event.

impartial: "The category is what survives when the object is gone. We are building the category."
questActive: "Describe the mechanism. I don't need the names — I need the shape of what happened."
friendly: "Secondary acquisitions means I receive what primary collection cannot categorize. Most of what I hold is things that shouldn't exist."
dearFriend: "Stamped. Filed. The archive now contains something it didn't have yesterday — a record that something was lost by being read."

npcs.quote: I carried the last embassy from Priam to Achilles. I am the only one who returned.

meta.worldTruth: The herald's immunity is the only law that held in ten years of war.
meta.enemy: Those who killed heralds — there were three; none of them prospered.

impartial: "I carried the last embassy from Priam to Achilles. I am the only one who returned."
questActive: "The document must reach its destination. That is the whole of the herald's art."
friendly: "Priam sent me because I was old enough that killing me would have been embarrassing. That was the full extent of my protection."
dearFriend: "The embassy failed. We knew it would. We went anyway. That is what embassies are for."

npcs.quote: Helen asked me once if I regretted coming with her. I said: I came with my queen. That is not regret.

meta.worldTruth: Service outlasts the war and the kingdom and the name of the queen.
meta.enemy: Those who confuse loyalty with agreement.

impartial: "Helen asked me once if I regretted coming with her. I said: I came with my queen. That is not regret."
questActive: "The robe was hers. I carried it from the burning room. She would have wanted it carried."
friendly: "I have been attendant to three queens. Each of them thought her situation was unique. Each of them was right."
dearFriend: "The city fell. The robe survived. Someone had to carry it. That is the whole of my history."

npcs.quote: Achilles drove the chariot once, for a demonstration. After that he let me drive.

meta.worldTruth: The charioteer keeps the record because the warrior is too busy fighting to write it down.
meta.enemy: Those who claim they drove Achilles — there were none.

impartial: "Achilles drove the chariot once, for a demonstration. After that he let me drive."
questActive: "I wrote the commission record. The only written record of what passed between us. I kept it."
friendly: "He never thanked me. He wasn't built for it. He did trust me with the horses, which is the same thing, in that world."
dearFriend: "The horses mourned him. Real mourning — they stood still for a day. I didn't know horses did that until then."

npcs.quote: I carried the weaving from the burning room. Both hands. I have kept the burns.

meta.worldTruth: What survives a burning is what someone ran back for.
meta.enemy: Those who describe the sack of Troy without naming who carried things out.

impartial: "I carried the weaving from the burning room. Both hands. I have kept the burns."
questActive: "The weaving was hers. Andromache's. She would have gone back for it. I went first."
friendly: "A slave's name is written nowhere in the record of Troy. I know what I carried. That is my record."
dearFriend: "She saw the burns and said nothing. She knew what they were. That was enough."

npcs.quote: I move. I remember the path. I do not require rest. That is what Hephaestus built me for.

meta.worldTruth: The mechanical servant keeps the record the organic servant cannot hold without sleeping.
meta.enemy: Those who assume the scroll is decorative.

impartial: "I move. I remember the path. I do not require rest. That is what Hephaestus built me for."
questActive: "The shield description is in my custody. I have held it since the forge. I will hold it until instructed otherwise."
friendly: "The gods made me to be useful. I have been useful for longer than most things that were made to be useful."
dearFriend: "I was given one instruction: hold the scroll. I have held it. You are the first to ask what is on it."

npcs.quote: I walked out of Troy carrying Hecuba's robe. The robe is why I walked.

meta.worldTruth: Survival requires a reason to carry something. The object becomes the reason.
meta.enemy: Those who left empty-handed and called it wisdom.

impartial: "I walked out of Troy carrying Hecuba's robe. The robe is why I walked."
questActive: "It must reach the archive. It has been carried this far. Do not let it stop here."
friendly: "The fire was everywhere. I had ten seconds to decide what to take. I took the thing that could not be rebuilt."
dearFriend: "The queen's robe survived the burning of Troy. Someone will read that sentence in two hundred years and not know my name. That is correct."

npcs.quote: I recognized the scar before he said a word. I have kept every secret since.

meta.worldTruth: The housekeeper knows the household before the master returns to it.
meta.enemy: Suitors who treated the hall as their own — none of them understood what they were in.

impartial: "I recognized the scar before he said a word. I have kept every secret since."
questActive: "The tally is accurate. Every jar, every measure, every day they were in the hall. It is all here."
friendly: "I nursed him as a child. I kept the house twenty years. I knew his step before I saw his face."
dearFriend: "The tally covers twenty years. I kept it because I knew he would return and would want to know exactly what was taken. He did return. He did want to know."

meta.worldTruth: The lake is the same every day. The fish are not.

questActive: "...Nice Day For Fishing. Yugurt! ...Nice Day For Fishing. Yugurt!"
friendly: "You got the shark. That's a different kind of fishing." He looks back at the lake.
dearFriend: "First Circle used to say the archive outlasts the archivist." He drinks. "...Nice Day For Fishing. Yugurt."
